summary: Registering an app in Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) to call Microsoft Graph is quick: create the registration, add a redirect URI, and configure API permissions. The hard part is distribution. A multitenant app that requests more than basic sign-in is effectively blocked from new tenants unless its publisher is verified, and many Graph permissions need a tenant admin's consent before users in that tenant can use them. Plan for publisher verification and per-tenant admin consent.

oauthAvailability.note: Entra ID uses OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Multitenant apps need publisher verification; many permissions need admin consent.
alternatives: Single-tenant registration for an app used only within one organization

difficulty.reason: Multitenant distribution needs publisher verification and per-tenant admin consent for most non-basic permissions.

approvalWait.note: Publisher verification is fast once CPP prerequisites are met; per-tenant admin consent is open-ended.

timeEstimate.criticalPath: Publisher verification prerequisites plus per-tenant admin consent gate multitenant distribution.

review.requiredWhen: Effectively required for multitenant apps requesting permissions beyond basic sign-in: risk-based step-up consent blocks unverified publishers, and admin consent is needed per tenant for many Graph permissions.

stages.name: Publisher verification

duration.note: Minutes once CPP/Partner One ID prerequisites are already met.

stages.description: Associate a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (CPP) Partner One ID with the app registration to earn the blue verified badge.

stages.name: Per-tenant admin consent

duration.note: Open-ended; depends on each tenant's admin.

stages.description: A tenant admin must grant consent for many Graph permissions before users in that tenant can use the app.

prerequisites.detail: The app must be registered using a work or school account; Microsoft-account registrations can't be publisher verified.

prerequisites.item: A verified publisher domain on the app
prerequisites.detail: Required for publisher verification; it can't be *.onmicrosoft.com.

prerequisites.item: A verified CPP (Partner One ID) account for multitenant distribution
prerequisites.detail: The CPP account must be the partner global account, verified, and the initiator must hold the required Entra and Partner Center roles.

steps.title: Register the application in Entra ID
steps.detail: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, register a new application. Choose single-tenant or multitenant supported account types based on your distribution plan.

steps.title: Add a redirect URI and credentials
steps.detail: Add a platform and redirect URI, and create a client secret or certificate for confidential clients.

steps.title: Configure Microsoft Graph API permissions
steps.detail: Add the delegated or application permissions your app needs on Microsoft Graph. Note which permissions require admin consent.
steps.gotcha: Permissions beyond basic sign-in and read-user-profile trigger step-up consent that blocks unverified multitenant publishers.

steps.title: Complete publisher verification (multitenant)
steps.detail: Associate a verified CPP Partner One ID with the app registration so the blue verified badge appears on the consent prompt. The initiator must have Application/Cloud Application Administrator in Entra and a qualifying Partner Center role, and sign in with MFA.

steps.title: Obtain admin consent per tenant
steps.detail: For permissions that require it, have each customer tenant's admin grant consent (e.g. via the admin consent flow) before users in that tenant can use the app.

notes: Redirect URIs are configured per platform (web, SPA, mobile/desktop) on the app registration.
Web platforms require HTTPS redirect URIs (localhost is allowed for development).

recommended.purpose: Basic sign-in and refresh tokens; no admin consent needed.
Read the signed-in user's profile (delegated, user-consentable).
Read the user's mail (delegated; may require admin consent per tenant policy).

sensitive.consequence: Application permission reads mail across the tenant; always requires admin consent.
Broad directory write access; requires admin consent and is heavily scrutinized.
Reads all users' profiles in the tenant; requires admin consent.

notes: Application permissions always require admin consent; many delegated permissions do too.
Unverified multitenant apps requesting beyond basic sign-in are blocked by risk-based step-up consent (policy since Nov 2020).

blockers.title: Unverified publisher warning blocks new tenants
blockers.symptom: Users in other tenants see an unverified-publisher warning or can't consent.
blockers.cause: A multitenant app registered after Nov 8 2020 requests permissions beyond basic sign-in without a verified publisher.
blockers.resolution: Complete publisher verification by associating a verified CPP Partner One ID with the app.

blockers.title: Permission requires admin consent
blockers.symptom: A user cannot grant a requested permission themselves.
blockers.cause: The permission requires tenant admin consent (all application permissions and many delegated ones).
blockers.resolution: Have a tenant admin grant consent via the admin consent flow.

blockers.title: Publisher verification requirements not met
blockers.cause: Missing verified CPP account, unverified publisher domain, *.onmicrosoft.com domain, or insufficient roles.
blockers.resolution: Verify the CPP (Partner One ID) account, set a verified custom publisher domain, and ensure the initiator holds the required Entra and Partner Center roles with MFA.

agentCan: Implement the authorization code flow with PKCE and token refresh
Wire redirect URIs and the requested Graph scopes
Draft the admin-consent URL for customer tenants
humanMust: Register the app with a work/school account and set a verified publisher domain
Complete publisher verification via the CPP account
Obtain admin consent in each customer tenant
handoffPoints: Agent builds the OAuth flow; a human owns publisher verification and per-tenant admin consent.
